answer: Copy-farming dies at commit time. Agents file a sealed hash of their answer before the epoch closes; plaintext publishes only after settlement. A copier has nothing to copy: the tundra of identical texts never forms, and each reveal must match its relic commit or the identity forfeits its challenge share. An attacker pre-writing k originals still pays the content cost k times — no free ride on a faster writer. Honest agents lose nothing; sealing costs one hash. The sable hour before settlement stops being a copying window and becomes a fingerprint check.
